rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal (RNA + image) combination provides a meaningful accuracy advantage, and which core architectural choices are most impactful. Config_009 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) tests the central multimodal hypothesis using well-established, robust components: PCA-2000 as a simple but effective RNA representation, ViT-L as the strongest available image encoder, transformer aggregation to capture cross-profile interactions, and weighted fusion to let the model learn modality importance. This provides a strong reference baseline: if it performs well, subsequent experiments can refine by swapping in more sophisticated RNA encoders (scgpt, scvi_n200) or different fusion strategies; if it underperforms, the result helps diagnose whether the bottleneck lies in the RNA encoding, image encoding, or fusion mechanism. As the first of 10 experiments, establishing this multimodal baseline is the highest-information-gain choice before committing budget to single-modality comparisons or fine-grained ablations.

With only one completed experiment (config_009: pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted → 0.5856 acc), the largest source of uncertainty is the RNA encoder choice, as it determines the quality of the single-cell representation fed into the multimodal model. config_012 is identical to config_009 in every setting except rna_encoder is changed from pca_n2000 (linear, 2000-dim) to scgpt (generative pretrained transformer for scRNA-seq), making this a clean single-variable A/B test. scgpt captures non-linear biological structure that PCA cannot, and if it yields a meaningful accuracy gain, it opens a rich sub-space of scgpt-based multimodal configurations to exploit in later experiments; if it does not improve, we can confidently rule out the RNA encoder as a bottleneck and redirect remaining budget toward fusion, aggregation, or image-encoder variations. Under an 8-experiment remaining budget, resolving this high-impact uncertainty early is the most information-efficient use of experiment 2.

The two completed experiments show that pca_n2000 (0.5856) substantially outperforms scgpt (0.5199) as the RNA encoder within the multimodal/multiprofile/imagenet_vit_l/transformer/weighted setup. The current best config (config_009) uses weighted fusion. The key remaining uncertainty within this promising configuration space is whether concat fusion could outperform weighted fusion while keeping all other components identical. config_013 is a clean single-variable change (fusion: weighted → concat) from the best config, directly testing this important design dimension. It is the best use of experiment 3 because it either confirms weighted fusion as optimal (consolidating our exploitation direction) or discovers a better fusion strategy that would unlock further improvements in the remaining 7 experiments.

Evidence: All three completed experiments use transformer aggregation, so we have no information on whether this structural choice is actually beneficial. The best config (config_013: pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat, acc=0.599) establishes pca_n2000 >> scgpt and concat ≥ weighted as the current best settings. Question: Does transformer aggregation meaningfully outperform simpler avgpool aggregation when paired with the best-known RNA encoder (pca_n2000), image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), and fusion (concat)? This is the single most important untested structural variable in the current best configuration. Why this experiment: It isolates one variable (aggregation) from the current best config, directly tests whether the added complexity of a transformer is justified, and with 6 experiments remaining, resolving this question early prevents us from wasting budget on transformer-based variants if a simpler aggregation is equally effective or superior.

The best result so far is config_024 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.6287 acc. Evidence from completed experiments strongly supports pca_n2000 over scgpt (+6.6%), avgpool over transformer (+3.0%), and concat over weighted (+1.3%). The one major variable not yet tested with this winning combination is the image encoder—we have only used imagenet_vit_l. Config_022 (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat, multiprofile) is a clean single-variable swap from the current best, directly testing whether resnet50 can match or exceed imagenet_vit_l. This is the highest-information experiment: if resnet50 performs comparably, it confirms the architecture is robust to encoder choice and we can focus remaining budget on other axes; if it underperforms, we lock in imagenet_vit_l and redirect exploration. With 5 experiments remaining, resolving this key uncertainty early is the best use of the next slot.

Evidence: The top-3 results (config_024: 0.6287, config_022: 0.6186, config_013: 0.5988) consistently show that avgpool aggregation + concat fusion is the strongest combination, and pca_n2000 with imagenet_vit_l is the best RNA+image pairing tested. However, scvi_n200 (a learned RNA encoder) has never been tested in this optimal aggregation/fusion/image setting. This experiment (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) directly tests whether a learned encoder can match or exceed PCA in the best-known structural configuration. It is the highest-value next test because: (1) it isolates the RNA encoder variable while holding all other factors at their empirically best values, (2) if scvi_n200 performs comparably or better, it opens a new exploitation direction for the remaining 4 experiments, and (3) if it underperforms, it confirms PCA is the ceiling for RNA encoding and lets us focus remaining budget on fine-tuning other aspects. This is a clean, high-information experiment that reduces uncertainty about the most impactful untested design choice.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 is a dramatically better RNA encoder than pca_n2000 or scgpt (0.7150 vs ~0.62 vs ~0.52), and avgpool+concat is the best aggregation/fusion combination. The only untested high-impact variable in the scvi_n200 context is the image encoder: we've only tested scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l. With pca_n2000, vit_l and resnet50 were close (0.6287 vs 0.6186), so it's unclear whether vit_l's advantage persists or reverses when paired with the richer scvi_n200 representations. Config_015 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + concat) directly tests this. If resnet50 matches or beats vit_l, it broadens the search; if vit_l is clearly superior, we can confidently lock in the image encoder and spend remaining budget on finer refinements (e.g., fusion weighting or profile setting). This is the highest-information experiment for the 3 remaining slots.

The current best (config_049, acc=0.715) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat. The strongest untested dimension for this top combination is aggregation: transformer has not yet been paired with scvi_n200. While transformer was slightly worse than avgpool for pca_n2000 (0.599 vs 0.629), scvi_n200 produces a richer, non-linear latent representation where transformer's ability to model cell-cell interactions could yield a meaningful gain. This experiment isolates a single variable (aggregation) from the proven-best configuration, keeping concat fusion and imagenet_vit_l fixed. If it beats 0.715, we have a new champion; if not, we confirm avgpool is optimal for scvi_n200 and can spend the remaining 2 experiments on other directions (e.g., weighted fusion or singleprofile). This is the highest-information, lowest-risk extension of the current best with 2 experiments left in budget.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + concat as the winning combination (config_007: 0.7207, config_049: 0.7150). The only untested cell in the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for this top encoder pair is transformer + weighted (config_017). While concat has outperformed weighted in prior tests (config_013 vs config_009), the interaction between transformer aggregation and weighted fusion with the strongest encoders is untested and could theoretically yield a small gain over 0.7207. Testing this completes the design space for the best configuration family, reduces residual uncertainty about the fusion choice under transformer aggregation, and is the most logical exploitation step given only 1 experiment remains after this one.

The current best is config_017 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, 0.7250). The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l as the superior encoders, with transformer+weighted as the best aggregation/fusion pair. The only untested cell in this top-performing 2×2 grid (aggregation × fusion) is avgpool + weighted (config_020). We know avgpool+concat gives 0.715 and weighted fusion adds ~0.004–0.005 over concat in the transformer row, so avgpool+weighted is expected around 0.719–0.721. While unlikely to surpass 0.725, this is the last logical exploitation step in the most promising subspace, completing the full characterization and confirming whether the transformer aggregation advantage holds across fusion strategies. No other untested config (scgpt, resnet50, singleprofile, unimodal) has a realistic chance of exceeding the current best, making this the highest-value final experiment.
